7.0.0.en: The angel and Tobias reached the house of Raguel and went in to him, and he received them with welcome and joy. This shows that he possessed the virtue of hospitality to strangers, and so we see God's blessings upon the devout who love virtue. Raguel, by his love for all people and his hospitality to strangers among them, gained a great blessing in the solution of the problem of his life, namely the death of the husbands of his only daughter, for God sent him his devout relative Tobias to marry her and beget a righteous offspring. Thus everyone who strives to acquire a virtue is led by it to other virtues and abundant blessings from God, and it also lifts from him his various afflictions.

7.1.0.en: The acquaintance began between the members of the household and the guests, and before Raguel spoke with them, he noticed the great resemblance in appearance between the young man before him and his relative Tobit the father, and he whispered this to his wife Anna. The longer text of the book says that Raguel was the cousin of Tobit the father.

7.2.0.en: Then Raguel asked the two young men about their origin and where they lived, and they told him that they were of the captives of the tribe of Nephthali, who were carried away to the city of Nineveh, the capital of Assyria (see Map 2, p. 265).

7.3.0.en: Raguel asked at once: Do you know Tobit my brother? This makes clear that he was not merely a relative of his from his tribe and kindred, but also very dear to his heart, in addition to the spiritual and worldwide standing of Tobit the father. They answered that they knew him.

7.4.0.en: Raguel rejoiced and began to speak about his relative, whom he called my brother because of the closeness of the kinship, and to praise his many virtues. After much speaking about the virtues of Tobit, the angel said that this Tobit of whom you speak is the father of this young man before you, indicating the younger Tobias.

7.5.0.en: When Raguel heard that the young Tobias before him was the son of his beloved Tobit the father, and he had noticed the resemblance between them at the beginning of the meeting, he rejoiced greatly and hurried to embrace Tobias, and from the excess of his joy he wept much.

7.6.0.en: Anna wept too, and Sara likewise, and Raguel went on praising Tobias and blessed him, because he was the son of the righteous man of many virtues.

7.6.1.en: The younger Tobias is a type of Christ, who came down to our earth (the house of Raguel) by His Incarnation, and the devout received Him with joy, namely Joseph the carpenter with the Virgin Mary, and the shepherds and the Magi. After many days (the long conversation) which He spent on our earth, our redemption was accomplished on the Cross, to blot out the penalty of death due to us. Thus He bought us with His blood as a bride for Himself, that we might live with Him a new life, full of peace and joy forever. Sara also represents the Church condemned to death, whom Christ redeemed and who became His bride. The younger Tobias learned of Sara's problem and came to marry her, so that she might be delivered from her shame and begin a new life with him. In this he is a type of Christ, who knows our pains and the death decreed against us, and became incarnate and came to us and redeemed us on the Cross, to save us.

7.6.2.en: God feels for you and cares for your prayers and arranges your salvation at the proper time, to lift your pains from you, not only the bodily ones, but, more important, the salvation of your soul and your eternal life. So do not be troubled if the pains increase, or if the answer to your prayers is delayed.

7.7.1.en: After the warm meeting between Tobias and the family of Raguel, they sat and talked at length, each telling the other about his life, and they rejoiced at one another's news. Then Raguel ordered a ram to be slaughtered and the food prepared for the guests. The ram here points to the sacrifices of the Old Testament, whose blood was a type of the sacrifice of Christ, but the redemption had to be accomplished by the death of Christ Himself, that is, by the marriage of Tobias, who enters into death (the chamber) and binds Satan, and then comes out alive with his bride, the Church, to the new life.

7.8.0.en: Despite Raguel's great welcome, the embracing, the weeping and the preparation of the feast, Tobias was not distracted from his goal which the angel had charged him with, and he asked Raguel to give him his daughter in marriage. Tobias here represents the spiritual man, who is not distracted from his goal, which is eternity, by the vain pleasures of the world, or the servant who is not distracted from seeking the salvation of souls by the conversations and works of this world and its material necessities.

7.9.0.en: Raguel was afraid when he heard this and trembled. This shows Raguel's love for those around him; he was not selfish, for he gave up his joy in his daughter, thinking of the fate awaiting Tobias, his death, like the seven previous husbands.

7.10.0.en: While Raguel was afraid and hesitant, Azarias, whose name means God helps, helped him and reassured him to give his daughter to Tobias and that no harm would come to him. The death of the seven previous husbands was because they were wicked and lustful, while Tobias is the only one worthy to marry Sara, because he reveres God and fears Him. It is clear from this that whoever reveres God and fears Him receives many blessings, whereas whoever departs from God and is immersed in the lusts of the world loses God's protection of him and is exposed to the warfare of the devil and, in the end, to eternal perdition.

7.11.0.en: Raguel was assured in faith that God had answered his prayers and had at last sent a relative who feared God to marry his daughter, according to the Law of Moses, who commanded that the Jews marry among themselves and among relatives and not from the Gentiles, to preserve the land and the lineages. All these things were a preparation for the coming of the awaited Messiah, Jesus Christ our God, in whom all the types are fulfilled. Then he promised and reassured Tobias that he would give him Sara as a wife.

7.12.s.en: (2) The marriage of Tobias to Sara

7.12.0.en: The marriage ceremonies began, and Raguel took the hand of his daughter Sara and gave her to Tobias. This is still the practice today: the father of the bride gives her hand to her betrothed when they enter the church to complete the sacrament of Matrimony, and the priest also gives the bridegroom the hand of his bride before the sanctuary during the completion of the sacrament. In the Old Testament the head of the family performed the work of the priest (since marriage was not yet a sacrament and the sacraments had not yet been instituted).

7.13.0.en: After the marriage was completed spiritually, they wrote a marriage contract and signed it, as proof of what God had accomplished, and this is still in force today.

7.13.1.en: We note that nothing is said about the dowry, because Tobias was poor and had nothing to offer his bride except himself. He is a type of Christ, who became poor for our sake and offered Himself naked of all the glory of the world on the Cross, and gave Himself as redemption and salvation for His Church.

7.14.0.en: After the marriage was completed they rose and ate from the feast with joy. This often happens now: after the completion of the marriage a feast is held which the couple attend with relatives and loved ones, to express their joy in the work of God. These feasts must differ from the feasts of the people of the world, which are full of displays unsuitable for the children of God, for God's blessing in love feasts cannot agree with displays that anger Him.

7.14.1.en: The rite of the Church prefers that the crowning be held before the Divine Liturgy, after the raising of the morning incense, so that the bride and bridegroom may partake of the Holy Mysteries, because every sacrament is crowned with the sacrament of the Eucharist, which is the sacrament of sacraments. From here this feast is a symbol of the sacrament of the Eucharist, which takes place after the marriage.

7.15.0.en: After the feast, Raguel ordered a private dwelling to be prepared, that is, a suite including a chamber and its annexes, for the bride and bridegroom. This confirms the spiritual and psychological principle that newlyweds should have a separate dwelling, in which they can cooperate in forming a new family, enjoying oneness and privacy together with their love for their relatives. In ancient times houses were very large, allowing separate suites, like the buildings that exist today containing a group of apartments.

7.16.0.en: Sara went in with Tobias to her chamber with tears in her eyes. They were tears in which the joy of marriage mingled with fear for her bridegroom lest he die, and also tears of awe at the new life.

7.17.0.en: May He grant you: may He give you.

7.17.1.en: Anna, Sara's mother, sent her off with words of encouragement and wishes of hope for joy, in place of all her former troubles.

7.17.2.en: The mother, as she encourages her daughter Sara, is a type of the angel who encourages the Church. The Church is here represented in the person of Christ our God, who carried us in His body and was wrestling for our sake in the garden of Gethsemane, and His sweat was like drops of blood, like the tears of Sara falling from her eyes, and then an angel came to strengthen Him.

7.17.3.en: Tobias and Sara begin their married life

8.0.s.en: (1) The prayer of Tobias and Sara and the defeat of Satan

8.0.0.en: After the wedding feast, that is, the supper, Tobias the husband went into the chamber with his wife. This supper is a type of the Lord's Supper, which Christ held on Holy Thursday, in which He offered His Body and Blood as food for His disciples and His Church.

8.1.1.en: As soon as he went in, he remembered the angel's words, so he prepared coals and laid upon them a part of the liver of the fish and also its heart, although it is not mentioned in this verse, but it is understood from what came before (Tob 6:8). Here we see that Tobias uses something material to accomplish a spiritual work, for by the burning of the liver and the heart the angel Raphael bound Satan, as appears in (v. 3). This is what the Church does in her sacraments, taking a material form for the hidden spiritual work of the Holy Spirit: the renewal of man's nature in the sacrament of Baptism takes place under the form of water, and in the sacrament of the Eucharist we receive the Body and Blood of Christ under the form of bread and wine; for we are human beings of spirit and body, and we need something perceptible that the body can touch, while the spirit believes in the work of God.

8.1.2.en: Because of what Tobias did, kindling coals when he first entered his chamber with his wife, the Church has cared for the rite of blessing houses and raising incense, to sanctify the dwelling of the bride and bridegroom before their marriage and at every other time, to drive away the works of the demons and for the blessing of God to come.

8.2.1.en: Then the devil Asmodeus could not approach them, and more than this, the archangel Raphael attacked him and seized him and cast him into the desert of Upper Egypt, that is, the desert of the far Sa'id; for Egypt resisted the works of God in the form of Pharaoh and all his people and his soldiers, in the days when the people of God dwelt among them, and God struck them with the ten plagues. We see that demons like to dwell in the deserts far from men, since some of them have a relationship with God in prayer and worship, and Satan cannot bear prayers raised in humility and love of God. In addition, the desert of Upper Egypt, that is, the far Sa'id, is the region of Luxor, which was called Thebes, where the Egyptians worshiped the god Amun and many gods, and idols spread in this region, and there Satan rests; for the Psalm says: "All the gods of the nations are demons" (Ps 96:5). It is understood from this that what Tobias did is not among the works of magic, as some object to this book, because magic is among the works of the demons, but here the binding of Satan is among the works of God. Just as they accused Christ of having a relationship with Beelzebub, and He answered them that if a kingdom is divided against itself it is brought to desolation. So this cannot be a work of satanic magic, but the work of God, who is stronger than the demons and able to bind him (Mt 12:24-30). Thus the blessings of the obedience in which Tobias walked appear, and God rescued him from death. So we too, by our obedience to the commandments of God, are rescued by Him from eternal death.

8.2.2.en: The younger Tobias here is a type of Christ, and his meeting with Sara in the chamber, and the binding of Satan and his being cast far away in the desert of Egypt, is a type of what happened on the day of Christ's crucifixion. By His death He bound Satan and died for His Church, united with her, to raise her in Himself from death by the resurrection on the third day. This day we can call the day of Golgotha, or Great Friday, while the third day is the day of the Resurrection.

8.2.3.en: Raphael's seizing of Satan and casting him far from Sara and Tobias is a type of Christ's binding of Satan by His Cross and driving him away from His bride the Church.

8.2.4.en: May you sanctify your house with many prayers, so that the angels guard it and keep away from it all the deeds of the devil.

8.3.0.en: Tobias came forward, as the head of this new family and its leader, and spoke to his wife that they should stand to pray and enjoy union with God through prayer for three days, after the likeness of the Holy Trinity, that is, the perfection of oneness and communion with God. When they are united with God, they are able to be united bodily in a conjugal relationship. This is the conduct of the children of God who are sanctified in Him, where their relationship with God is the basis of all their works.

8.4.0.en: The couple rose and prayed a fervent prayer from the heart, that God would keep them in His love, and keep away from them all the works of the devil, and heal them of all spiritual illnesses, that is, forgive their sins.

8.5.0.en: The divine inspiration records for us here the prayer of Tobias and Sara, which is considered an excellent model that we offer to every bride and bridegroom at the beginning of their life, to follow it. Tobias raised his heart in praise to God before everything, calling all creation to glorify God with him. For so man was created to be lord of all creation and responsible for leading it in the praise of God.

8.6.0.en: Tobias remembered the first marriage in the world, in Paradise before the fall, that is, the marriage of Adam and Eve, wishing that his marriage might be in union with God and a relationship of love and continual prayer.

8.7.0.en: Then Tobias declares that lust was not the aim of their marriage, but the begetting of offspring, in whom God is blessed, and this offspring shares in the praise of God. The begetting of offspring in the Old Testament was an important matter, much more than in the New Testament, since everyone hoped that the Messiah would come from his offspring; therefore barrenness was a sign of weakness and lack of blessing. But in the New Testament, marriage is complete in its blessing, even without children; for spiritual sonship is more important, as is the service of God in addition to praise.

8.8.0.en: As for Sara, she prayed in humility, asking the mercy of God, that He would forgive their sins and uphold them throughout their lives, even to old age; for a long life was a sign of blessing in the Old Testament.

8.9.s.en: (2) The prayer of Raguel and Anna after the deliverance of Tobias

8.9.0.en: Throughout the wedding night, both Raguel and his wife Anna kept watch, anxious about Tobias lest he die like the previous husbands. At the crowing of the cock, that is, the time before dawn, before the rising of the daybreak, Raguel gathered some of his servants and workers, and they dug a grave beside the house in which to bury Tobias.

8.10.0.en: Raguel feared that what had befallen the previous husbands would befall Tobias, for he believed that Tobias's death was inevitable and that he could not avert it.

8.11.0.en: Therefore Raguel ordered a grave to be prepared for Tobias, then asked his wife Anna to send a maidservant to look at the couple in the chamber, for he had a hidden hope that God was able to rescue Tobias.

8.12.0.en: The maidservant returned to tell them that she had seen them safe, alive, sleeping quietly, so the parents rejoiced and thanked and blessed the Lord.

8.12.1.en: Raguel and Anna are a type of the women who saw the Lord Jesus in the tomb and made sure of His death, then at dawn on Sunday, while it was still dark, went to the tomb, and the angel, to whom the maidservant points, met them and told them the good news of the Resurrection. Tobias is a type, as we mentioned, of Christ, and Sara of His Church, which is His body, with which He entered into death and came out alive by His resurrection.

8.13.0.en: The parents offered a prayer of thanksgiving to God and called Him the God of Israel, that is, the God who is concerned for His people and His children, because His mercy is wide and He turns away from us the works of the demons, for He is the Almighty and can rescue us from all dangers.

8.14.0.en: And they asked for the couple that they might live with God in a life of thanksgiving, and offer before Him sacrifices of praise, that is, their reasonable worship, in holy prayers and worship, and that God might be glorified in them and they might be a sign to all peoples, for there is no other god on earth but the God of Israel.

8.15.s.en: (3) The feast of joy and Raguel's gifts to Tobias

8.15.0.en: After the announcement of the good news of the new life which God had bestowed on the couple, every trace of death had to be removed, so Raguel filled in the grave before dawn, which points to the Resurrection, for death had ended with the darkness of the night. The filling in of the grave also is a type of the end of the authority of Hades over the children of God, whom He raised with Himself, as the empty tomb was proof of the resurrection of Christ on the third day.

8.16.0.en: Then he asked his wife Anna to prepare a great feast, the details of which, as he mentioned them, declare the extent of his joy and also his wealth, and it was for all the loved ones, that they might rejoice in the work of God. He also asked her to prepare the needs of travel for the couple and those with them.

8.16.1.en: For the feast he ordered two cows, and the cow points to goodness, giving and motherhood, since it gives milk abundantly to its young. As for the ram, that is, the male of the sheep, it points to obedience. The number of two cows points to the fact that God's redemption and blessings are for both Jews and Gentiles, and to confirm the meaning. As for four rams, they point to the four corners of the earth, that is, the whole world. The symbolic meaning in this feast is that the blessings of God and His overflowing goodness are poured out abundantly on His obedient children, who are subject to Him throughout the world.

8.17.0.en: He begged and urged Tobias to stay with them two weeks, that they might rejoice together in the wonderful work of God and live in the joys of marriage, which represent the joys of the Resurrection and the appearances of the Lord Christ. Raguel asked Tobias to stay with him two weeks, and the seven days (a week) point to the completeness of the work of the Holy Spirit, and two weeks to confirm the meaning, that is, the completeness of joy in the work of the Holy Spirit in holy matrimony.

8.17.1.en: Tobias did not make light of Raguel's oath, so as not to anger God, who hates the breaking of an oath, and out of respect for the wish of Raguel his father-in-law.

8.18.0.en: Then Raguel gave Tobias and his daughter Sara half of his money and promised them the other half after his death, and even wrote a bond to this effect. This shows the extent of his love for the couple, his love of giving, and his non-attachment to money.

8.18.1.en: Thus the blessings of God appear, not only in keeping us from dangers, but He gives us spiritual and material blessings which we cannot imagine.

8.18.2.en: Azarias recovers the money from Gabael and invites him to the wedding
